entries.title: Sindicato de Maestros de Chicago obtiene la mitad de los escaños de la junta escolar, pero pierde la presidencia
entries.summary: <p>A pesar de haber sido ampliamente superados en gastos, los candidatos respaldados por el Sindicato de Maestros de Chicago (CTU) ganaron seis de 21 escaños en la junta escolar y iban adelante en cuatro más, probablemente suficiente para presentar una oposición formidable a los recortes, al cierre de escuelas y a otras medidas que consideran contrarias a su agenda progresista.</p><p>El candidato del CTU a la presidencia del consejo, Hilario Domínguez, perdió ante Jessica Biggs. Los candidatos no respaldados por el CTU ganaron nueve de los 10 escaños restantes, y en otra contienda un candidato ajeno al CTU iba adelante en una carrera demasiado reñida como para llamarla. Un bloque de 10 miembros del CTU bastaría para complicarle la vida a Biggs.</p><p>El mayor rival del CTU en esta contienda fue Michael Sacks, millonario y exasesor de Rahm Emanuel, y el grupo político Common Ground Collective, en el que Sacks inyectó $6.8 millones en los últimos dos meses. Common Ground Collective solo ganó tres de las contiendas disputadas, aunque el grupo respaldó además a cinco candidatos sin oposición.</p><div class="RichTextSidebarModule Enhancement" data-module data-align-center><a class="AnchorLink" id="module-c00000" name="module-c00000"></a> <div class="RichTextModule-items RichTextBody"><h3>La Voz Chicago WhatsApp</h3>Encuentra más noticias en nuestro canal de WhatsApp. <a class="Link" href="https://www.whatsapp.com/channel/0029Vb0XT1XCHDylm3rCs40P" target="_blank" ><b>Síguenos.</b></a></div> </div><p>Biggs recibió $1 millón de Sacks, pero no fue respaldada formalmente por Common Ground Collective. Con estos resultados, a Biggs le falta la mayoría de dos tercios necesaria para anular cualquier resolución que pueda aprobarse en la reunión de la junta de diciembre, donde los miembros en ejercicio votarán por última vez.</p><p>La actual junta escolar, la mitad de los cuales es nombrada por el alcalde Brandon Johnson y está alineada con el CTU, podría aprobar una moratoria sobre el cierre de escuelas e intentar atar las manos de la junta entrante en lo que respecta a futuros recortes.</p><p>El CTU no tuvo candidatos en cinco de las 20 contiendas distritales tras no presentar aspirantes en dos de esas carreras, mientras que tres de sus candidatos fueron excluidos de la boleta mediante impugnaciones de peticiones.</p><p>El CTU fue superado en gastos por una proporción de 4 a 1, con Sacks aportando más de $8 millones a las contiendas.</p><p>Biggs, actual miembro de la junta escolar y exdirectora, se presentó como una constructora de consensos y, durante la campaña, a menudo destacó su “amplia coalición” de apoyo, que incluye al Sindicato Internacional de Empleados de Servicios (SEIU), que representa al personal de apoyo en las Escuelas Públicas de Chicago (CPS).</p><p>Pero, incluso en su discurso de victoria, Biggs lanzó un sutil dardo contra la actual junta controlada por el CTU, diciendo “las familias están cansadas del caos y la incertidumbre”, dijo. “Quieren estabilidad, y quieren que esta junta vuelva a centrar su atención en nuestros estudiantes”, añadió. “Quieren escuelas en las que puedan confiar, maestros que estén apoyados y líderes que pongan a los niños primero”.</p><p>Y Biggs tendrá que lidiar con un sindicato de maestros fuerte que probablemente no esté contento con ella.</p><p>Common Ground Collective transmitió anuncios contra Domínguez que contenían medias verdades sobre una acusación de mala conducta y siguió repitiéndolas incluso después de que el inspector general de CPS <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/la-voz/2026/10/13/investigacion-de-presunto-contacto-inapropiado-de-candidato-a-presidente-junta-de-cps-y-una-menor-podria-concluir" target="_blank" >concluyera que las acusaciones no estaban fundamentadas</a>.</p><p>Biggs no se pronunció en contra de esos anuncios y se benefició de ellos —un hecho que los funcionarios del CTU y los miembros de la junta recordarán probablemente al valorar trabajar con Biggs y sus aliados. Domínguez, que estaba de licencia en su puesto como subdirector político del CTU, probablemente regresará a su cargo con recelo hacia Biggs.</p><p>Muchos expertos dicen que Sacks se involucró tanto porque vio la elección de la junta escolar como un indicador de la carrera por la alcaldía en febrero. Sacks y el mundo empresarial ya han aportado mucho dinero a Alexi Giannoulias, a quien esperan que pueda derrotar a Johnson.</p><p>Una actuación mejor de lo esperado por parte del sindicato de maestros podría ser un buen augurio para Johnson. Pero, en general, los sindicatos de maestros tienden a que les vaya bien en las elecciones de juntas escolares, dijo Jeffrey R. Henig, profesor emérito del Teachers College de la Universidad de Columbia, quien coescribió un libro sobre el dinero externo en las elecciones de consejos escolares.</p><p>Los votantes confían en que los maestros saben lo que debería estar pasando en las escuelas, y también desprecian a los forasteros que intentan imponer su voluntad, dijo.</p><p>“En las elecciones de las juntas escolares y en otras elecciones estatales y locales, los candidatos han podido derrotar a personas con mayores presupuestos de campaña, señalando con el dedo y diciendo: ‘Esta persona está siendo financiada por multimillonarios que no invierten en la educación pública’”, dijo Henig.</p><h3>El presupuesto del distrito será la prioridad para la nueva junta</h3><p>Los miembros de la nueva junta escolar tomarán posesión el 15 de enero. Pero lo que suceda en los próximos dos meses tendrá grandes consecuencias para el inicio de su mandato.</p><p>En julio, los miembros de la junta respaldados por el CTU votaron a favor de un presupuesto que <a class="Link" href="https://www.wbez.org/education/chicago-school-board/2026/07/30/chicago-school-board-approves-budget-that-reverses-layoffs-but-counts-on-shaky-state-funds" target="_blank" >cuenta con $150 millones en ingresos no comprometidos por parte del Estado</a>. Hicieron esto para reincorporar a algunos de los más de 1,000 maestros y otro personal que fueron <a class="Link" href="https://www.wbez.org/education/chicago-school-board/2026/07/15/cps-will-cut-teachers-and-five-student-non-attendance-days-as-district-looks-to-close-budget-deficit" target="_blank" >despedidos a principios del verano</a> para cerrar el déficit de $732 millones de CPS.</p><p>Sin embargo, la legislatura estatal no ha aprobado fondos adicionales y no volverá a Springfield hasta la sesión de vetos de la próxima semana. La presidenta del CTU, Stacy Davis Gates, dijo que, independientemente de quién ganara la elección, ella y otros estarán en Springfield para luchar por ese dinero.</p><p>Aun así, si no llega, la nueva junta escolar probablemente tendrá que ingeniárselas para recortar gastos y equilibrar el presupuesto de CPS. No está claro exactamente cuánto se descompensaría el presupuesto del distrito sin la financiación estatal adicional.</p><p><a class="Link" href="https://www.chalkbeat.org/chicago/2026/10/01/teachers-and-school-leaders-navigate-uncertainty-as-layoffs-are-reversed/" target="_blank" >A principios de octubre, Chalkbeat Chicago informó</a> que CPS había vuelto a contratar sólo a 350 maestros. Si eso se mantiene, sería un costo adicional de $35 millones, mucho menos que los $150 millones añadidos por la junta.</p><p>Aun así, si hay un agujero significativo, la nueva junta tendrá que decidir cómo cerrarlo. Eso podría significar recurrir a suspensiones de personal sin goce de sueldo o despidos a mitad de año.</p><p>Pero Hal Woods, jefe de políticas de la organización de defensa Kids First, dijo que no cree que algunos miembros de la junta comprendan cuán limitadas son sus opciones.</p><p>“¿Van a recortar maestros? ¿Van a recortar asistentes?”, comentó. “Cuando tienes maestros y padres que vienen a la reunión de la junta diciendo: ‘Están recortando mi escuela’, eso pone a los miembros de la junta en una posición difícil”.</p><p><i>Traducido con una herramienta de inteligencia artificial (IA) y editado por los seres humanos de </i><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/la-voz" target="_blank" ><i>La Voz Chicago</i></a><br></p>

entries.title: Late Bears matriarch Virginia McCaskey a contributor finalist for Hall of Fame
entries.summary: <p>Late <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2025/02/06/virginia-mccaskey-bears-obit-dies-102-halas" target="_blank" >Bears</a> matriarch <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Virginia McCaskey</a> is one of five contributors who have advanced for a Pro Football Hall of Fame vote.</p><p>The list of five contributor finalists was whittled down from 42 nominees, the Hall said in a release Wednesday. The contributor subcommittee will meet virtually Nov. 17 to pick one of the five candidates to present to the full selection committee for enshrinement. They would very likely be approved.</p><p>McCaskey ran the Bears after her father George Halas’ death in 1983. She died Feb. 6, 2025, at 102. Halas founded the Bears and the NFL — the Hall is located on George Halas Drive.</p><p>The four other finalists are:</p><p>• Patriots owner Robert Kraft, whose teams have won six Super Bowls and played in five more.</p><p>• Doug Williams, who became the first black quarterback to start and win the Super Bowl as a player for Washington.</p><p>• John Wooten, a former NFL player and executive who later ran the Fritz Pollard Alliance, which worked to advance minority coaching and front office candidates.</p><p>• And Ralph Hay, the former Canton Bulldogs owner who hosted a meeting that formed the NFL at his car dealership in Canton.</p><p>The Class of 2027, which includes up to five players in addition to one coach and one contributor, will be announced at NFL Honors in Los Angeles during Super Bowl week.</p>

entries.title: Every known federal prosecution in Chicago tied to Trump’s immigration blitz
entries.summary: <p>Federal prosecutors in Chicago have accused 33 known defendants of nonimmigration crimes tied to Operation Midway Blitz. Many were accused of assaulting or resisting federal agents or officers.</p><p>Two defendants have pleaded guilty. Twenty-eight have been cleared. Grand jurors refused to indict at least three of the 28, and another member of that group was found not guilty at trial.</p><p>Four of the 28 saw their charges dropped through a deferred-prosecution agreement. Under the terms of such a deal, prosecutors agree to drop charges if a defendant abides by certain terms over a set period of time. Six Midway Blitz defendants struck such a deal, and two are still pending.</p><p>The Chicago Sun-Times is tracking all of the known criminal cases tied to Operation Midway Blitz:</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="HtmlModule"><a class="AnchorLink" id="html-embed-module-6e0000" name="html-embed-module-6e0000"></a><div class="flourish-embed flourish-table" data-src="visualisation/27349648"><script src="https://public.flourish.studio/resources/embed.js"></script><noscript><img src="https://public.flourish.studio/visualisation/27349648/thumbnail" width="100%" alt="table visualization" /></noscript></div> </div> </div><div class="PageListO" data-module data-show-loadmore="true" ><a class="AnchorLink" id="list-bb0000" name="list-bb0000"></a> <div class="PageList-header" > <div class="PageList-header-title-wrap" > <div class="PageList-header-title"> Latest from Jon Seidel </div> </div> </div> <div class="PageListO-items"> <div class="PageListO-items-row"> <div class="PageListO-items-column" data-with-borders> <div class="PageListO-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/11/02/fbi-boutros-depodesta-broadview-six" >'Broadview 6' case heats up again as ex-FBI boss sues, top federal prosecutor ordered to testify</a> </div> <div class="PageListO-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/politics/2026/11/02/broadview-six-boutros-perry" >Chicago's top federal prosecutor ordered to testify under oath in 'Broadview 6' case</a> </div> <div class="PageListO-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/politics/2026/11/02/broadview-six-depodesta-boutros-kat-abughazaleh" >Former FBI boss’ lawsuit undermines Boutros’ denial of Washington’s role in ‘Broadview 6’ case</a> </div> </div> </div> </div> </div><p></p>

entries.title: Jessica Biggs gana la presidencia de la Junta de Educación de Chicago
entries.summary: <p>La exdirectora de una escuela de las Escuelas Públicas de Chicago (CPS) y actual integrante de la Junta de Educación, Jessica Biggs, se declaró vencedora el martes, superando a dos rivales tras una campaña encendida para convertirse en la primera presidenta electa de la Junta de Educación de Chicago.</p><p>Obtuvo el 49% de los votos, con el 94% de las casillas contadas, según resultados de la Associated Press.</p><p>Hilario Domínguez, candidato respaldado por el Sindicato de Maestros de Chicago (CTU), quedó detrás de Biggs con casi el 31% de los votos, y el abogado Victor Henderson obtuvo el 17%.</p><div class="RichTextSidebarModule Enhancement" data-module data-align-center><a class="AnchorLink" id="module-860000" name="module-860000"></a> <div class="RichTextModule-items RichTextBody"><h3>La Voz Chicago WhatsApp</h3>Encuentra más noticias en nuestro canal de WhatsApp. <a class="Link" href="https://www.whatsapp.com/channel/0029Vb0XT1XCHDylm3rCs40P" target="_blank" ><b>Síguenos.</b></a></div> </div><p>Domínguez no había concedido la noche del martes, pero Biggs se dirigió a sus simpatizantes como presidenta electa de la junta escolar. Prometió centrarse en mejorar el aprendizaje de los estudiantes y en construir una coalición con socios estatales para conseguir más fondos para CPS, además de proteger a los estudiantes de los "ataques" del presidente Donald Trump.</p><p>"El camino por delante no será fácil", dijo Biggs. "Los retos que enfrenta nuestro distrito son enormes. Desde nuestras finanzas y la matrícula, hasta la confianza que debemos reconstruir con las familias. Pero nuestra determinación es igual de grande. Y esta noche, Chicago ha demostrado hasta qué punto la ciudad está dispuesta a luchar por sus niños”.</p><p>Biggs agradeció la "amplia coalición" que dijo haber logrado reunir, y reconoció a sus "donantes grandes y pequeños". Su victoria, afirmó Biggs, representa un triunfo para los residentes de Chicago, quienes ahora tienen voz en la dirección del distrito.</p><p>"Durante demasiado tiempo las decisiones sobre nuestras escuelas se han tomado a puerta cerrada en el Ayuntamiento, y las familias han tenido que vivir con las consecuencias, pero esta noche eso cambia", aseguró Biggs. "Nunca olvidaré para quién trabajo".</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item"> <bsp-carousel class="Carousel Enhancement" data-align-center> <a class="AnchorLink" Iba detrás de Jessica Biggs, pero no concedió.</p></figcaption><span class="line"></span><div class="Figure-credit"><p>Mark Black/Para el Sun-Times</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>Henderson tampoco concedió porque, como abogado, está "en eso de poner los puntos sobre las íes y [mirar todo con lupa]", dijo Henderson a sus simpatizantes en un restaurante del Near West Side. "Agradezco a cada uno de ustedes por estar aquí, por apoyarme".</p><p>Ahora Biggs tiene la tarea de asumir esta posición poderosa, aunque no remunerada, y de trabajar con otros 20 miembros para fijar una visión y metas para CPS durante los próximos cuatro años. Representará públicamente a la junta, liderará las reuniones mensuales y ayudará a establecer la agenda de un organismo que supervisa un presupuesto anual de alrededor de $10,000 millones.</p><p>La gran mayoría del dinero que inundó la elección de la junta escolar se concentró en la contienda por la presidencia, dado el influjo que tiene ese cargo. De los más de <a class="Link" href="https://graphics-stage.suntimes.com/esb/school-board/money/#mm-president" target="_blank" >$8.3 millones recaudados directamente por los candidatos</a>, $5.2 millones se han reunido en la elección de la presidencia, incluidos montos de dos candidatos que se retiraron. Biggs recaudó cerca de $1.9 millones, Domínguez $1.7 millones y Henderson unos $700,000, casi todo ese dinero se lo prestó él mismo.</p><p>Cuando se incluye el gasto de los super PACs, que no pueden coordinarse con los candidatos, se han gastado $13.9 millones en apoyar u oponerse a candidatos, según un análisis del Sun-Times y WBEZ. Esto incluye $3.5 millones para oponerse a Domínguez por parte de grupos que no quieren que el candidato del CTU lidere la junta. Los PAC financiados por el CTU han gastado apenas $577,000 en apoyo a su campaña.</p><p>Una de las primeras tareas de Biggs cuando asuma la presidencia de la junta en enero —y de la junta que presidirá— podría ser enfrentar un déficit presupuestario importante. El presupuesto de este año depende de que los legisladores en Springfield consigan fondos adicionales durante una sesión de veto a finales de este mes. El gobernador desestimó esa posibilidad la semana pasada.</p><p>Biggs se postuló como una líder capaz de construir consenso entre una amplia coalición. Sus simpatizantes incluían al sindicato progresista Service Employees International Union (SEIU) Local 73, que representa mayormente a trabajadores de CPS de bajos salarios, negros y latinos. Pero también recibió $1 millón de Sacks, quien ha estado en la mira del alcalde Brandon Johnson y del CTU. Biggs además contó con el apoyo de la comunidad empresarial y de exfuncionarios que trabajaron bajo la administración del exalcalde Rahm Emanuel.</p><p>Domínguez fue el escogido del CTU, con la esperanza de que pudiera liderar mientras el poderoso sindicato intenta mantener el control mayoritario de la junta. Domínguez es el exsubdirector político del sindicato. Está de licencia del CTU y de su puesto como maestro de educación especial en CPS.</p><p>Se postuló con una plataforma progresista que incluía ampliar la educación preescolar para todos los niños de 3 años y ampliar los servicios que brindan las escuelas para incluir clínicas de salud y tiendas de comestibles. LaRiviere/Sun-Times</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>Los tres candidatos dijeron que podrían convencer a los legisladores estatales de asignar más fondos a CPS, que sigue crónicamente subfinanciado. Durante el verano, la junta aprobó un presupuesto revisado que asumía $150 millones adicionales en fondos aún no comprometidos por el estado para evitar recortes que habrían afectado las aulas. Los miembros de la junta que apoyaron la medida prometieron presionar a los legisladores para que consiguieran el dinero este otoño.</p><p>Pero el gobernador JB Pritzker dijo el mes pasado que no ha habido conversaciones entre los legisladores sobre aportar fondos al distrito.</p><p>"No estoy seguro de que a mitad de año podamos hacer algo que satisfaga únicamente las necesidades de un distrito escolar", dijo Pritzker.</p><p>Los $150 millones en deuda estatal asumida se redujeron a $110 millones después de que el alcalde Brandon Johnson presentó su plan presupuestario en octubre. El plan incluye $286 millones de financiamiento por incremento tributario (TIF) destinados a CPS. Pero tampoco hay garantía de que esa cantidad se materialice por completo.</p><p>Si el distrito no recibe más fondos de la Ciudad o del Estado, podría verse obligado a recortar gastos a mitad de año o a pedir préstamos.</p><p>Pero incluso después de resolver los problemas presupuestarios de este año, Biggs, como nueva presidenta, tendrá que abordar los problemas financieros a largo plazo del distrito, así como otros asuntos, como la disminución de la matrícula.</p><p>CPS necesita $1.9 mil millones más del Estado para proporcionar una educación adecuada, según la fórmula estatal de financiamiento, y el distrito escolar se aleja cada vez más de la suficiencia. CPS ahora solo cuenta con el 70% de lo que necesita para alcanzar un financiamiento adecuado, comparado al 73% del año pasado y al 79% del anterior.</p><p>Al mismo tiempo, el distrito está educando a menos niños. La matrícula de CPS disminuyó en 11,500 estudiantes este año, hasta 304,700, la cifra más baja en más de dos décadas. La caída continúa una tendencia descendente que ocurre desde hace 20 años. Eso ha reavivado las conversaciones sobre cierres de escuelas.</p><p>Todos los candidatos salen de una campaña dolorosa que se intensificó en la recta final mientras cada uno enfrentaba controversias. Los votantes fueron bombardeados con anuncios negativos que destacaban los problemas en línea y por aire.</p><p>A Biggs se le cuestionaron sus acciones como directora y si hubo un quid pro quo con la directora ejecutiva de CPS, la superintendente Macquline King, para salir de la lista de no contratar del distrito, lo que ella niega rotundamente.</p><p>A Henderson se le plantearon preguntas sobre alegaciones durante sus trámites de divorcio hace 15 años. A Domínguez se le imputaron acusaciones sobre su conducta con una adolescente hace casi una década. La oficina del inspector general de CPS desde entonces <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/la-voz/2026/10/13/investigacion-de-presunto-contacto-inapropiado-de-candidato-a-presidente-junta-de-cps-y-una-menor-podria-concluir" target="_blank" >cerró una investigación</a> sobre esas acusaciones y determinó que no había pruebas suficientes de conducta indebida.</p><p><i>Contribuyeron: Lisa Kurian Philip, Kristen Schorsch y Araceli Gómez-Aldana </i></p><p><i>Traducido con una herramienta de inteligencia artificial (IA) y editado por los seres humanos de </i><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/la-voz" target="_blank" ><i>La Voz Chicago</i></a><br></p>

entries.title: Blue tsunami raises Democrats' already massive advantages in the Illinois General Assembly
entries.summary: <p>Democrats’ nationwide blue tsunami swept through Springfield on Tuesday night, too, running up the state party's super majorities toward historic highs in the Illinois General Assembly.</p><p>While facing criticism from within his own caucus for <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/springfield/2026/08/05/welch-benton-harassment-working-group-cassidy" target="_blank" ><u>his handling of sexual harassment allegations</u></a> by a former member, House Speaker Emanuel “Chris” Welch’s political operation flexed its muscle to flip at least four districts on Election Day.</p><p>By Wednesday morning, three additional House seats <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/graphics/voter-guide-midterm-election-illinois/illinois-midterm-results-2026/#legislature" target="_blank" >were still in play for Democrats</a>, potentially paving the way to a staggering 85-33 advantage for Welch’s party.</p><p>Democrats have held a 78-40 House advantage over Republicans under Welch’s leadership since 2022, already the largest in modern history on a starkly gerrymandered political map.</p><p>Illinois Senate President Don Harmon was poised to expand the hefty Democratic edge in the upper chamber as well, grabbing four new seats across the state and potentially two more that would increase their dominance to 46-13.</p><p>With Democratic blowouts in favor of Gov. JB Pritzker, Attorney General Kwame Raoul, Comptroller-elect Margaret Croke and <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/11/03/governor-illinois-jb-pritzker-darren-bailey-collin-corbett-results" target="_blank" ><u>all other statewide office-holders</u></a>, Illinois Republicans find themselves in their bleakest position in recent memory.</p><p>Among the Democratic spoils was state Rep. Nabeela Syed’s victory over incumbent Republican state Sen. Darby Hills for the northwest suburban 26th Senate District seat, a $6.5 million contest that marked <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/11/03/illinois-house-midterm-results" target="_blank" ><u>one of the most expensive in state history</u></a>.</p><p>But Democrats were also making inroads in territory long considered solid Republican ground, including the Rockford seat held by GOP state Sen. Dave Syverson since 1993. Democratic challenger Sarah Mertens held a narrow edge with 85% of expected votes counted by Wednesday morning.</p><p>The Welch-controlled Democrats for the Illinois House political committee raised some $35 million to tighten its grip on the Capitol.</p><p>He’ll still face a battle to hold onto the speaker’s gavel in January, as several members of his caucus have begun organizing behind closed doors to name a new speaker in the wake of Welch’s handling of misconduct allegations leveled against former Plainfield state Rep. Harry Benton. Democrats <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/11/03/us-illinois-house-97-midterm-results" target="_blank" ><u>still held onto that 97th District seat</u></a> with the help of a $1.6 million infusion from Welch’s operation.</p><p>Welch called their big night across the board “a testament to the strength of our members, the dedication of our campaigns, and the voters who continue to place their trust in House Democrats.”</p><p>“We set out to protect our incumbents, expand our majority, and make sure members had the resources necessary to compete and win,” Welch said in a statement. “Our historic supermajority is not just a reflection of electoral success. It is a mandate to continue delivering meaningful results for the people of Illinois.”</p><p>“The people of Illinois expect us to govern, to lead, and to deliver,” Welch added. “We will continue doing exactly that. Our majority is stronger, our caucus is growing, and our commitment to building a better Illinois has never been greater.”</p><p>Illinois Senate President Don Harmon said they reached "an overwhelming victory for Democrats because we've been focused on what matters to voters. We've fought to lower costs, improve healthcare, and stop the Trump administration in its tracks. We're excited to get back to work on behalf of the people with our new majority."</p><p>Political funds controlled by Harmon carried more than $32 million into the home stretch of the campaign season, dwarfing Republican war chests that have shrunk over the past decade with the exodus of conservative megadonors like Ken Griffin and Dick Uihlein.</p><p>The Illinois GOP has withered due largely to President Donald Trump’s <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/politics/2026/07/20/bob-grogan-illinois-republican-party-new-chairperson-dupage-county-auditor" target="_blank" ><u>deep unpopularity in suburban areas</u></a> that long provided the lifeblood of the state party.</p><p>But members of the hardline conservative Illinois Freedom Caucus, the fiercest Trump supporters in the General Assembly, suggested their party should respond to the bloodbath by leaning toward their pole.</p><p>“How much worse does it need to get before we try something new?” members of the downstate caucus said in a statement. “We are ready to unite as Republicans and look to the future, but we cannot ignore failure. Tonight was an absolute disaster. The 2028 election starts now. We look forward to hearing from our colleagues about their ideas for the future, because the only way to influence change is by winning elections.”</p>

entries.title: Joliet man accused of gunning down Chicago woman at Hammond Ind. Walmart
entries.summary: <p>The boyfriend of 21-year-old woman from Chicago who was killed during a shooting attack at a Hammond, Ind. Walmart, remains in custody Wednesday after being charged with her murder.</p><p>Dorian Kevon Robertson, 22, of Joliet, is being held at the Lake County Jail charged with first-degree murder in the slaying of Dakota Norwood, 21, according to Hammond police Cpt. Steve Kellogg.</p><p>Investigators determined that Norwood and the suspect knew each other and had been involved in a relationship, Kellogg said. The exact nature and length of that relationship remains under investigation, according to Kellogg.</p><p>At approximately 9:09 a.m. Monday, Hammond police were called to the Walmart, 1100 S. 5th Ave., store after an off-duty Hammond police officer working store security reported that a shooting had erupted and a suspect was in custody, according to Kellogg.</p><p>Norwood was working at the store when a conversation with Robertson, who she'd been in a relationship with, escalated into a physical altercation, Kellogg said.</p><p>Robertson allegedly retrieved a firearm and shot Norwood multiple times.</p><p>Norwood, of Chicago, was pronounced dead at 10:27 a.m. Monday, according to the Lake County coroner's office. An autopsy determined Norwood died of multiple gunshot wounds and her death was ruled a homicide.<br></p>

entries.title: Millions of American women don't want kids — one stands up to explain why
entries.summary: <p>The American birth rate has fallen to historic lows, and Bailey Swilley isn't helping any. Which is ironic.</p><p>"I love babies," said the Brooklyn-based comedian/storyteller. "That's the thing. I love babies. I like kids."</p><p>Fair enough. I love bread, yet don't want to be a baker.</p><p>"I don't see myself as a parent," she said. "I don't see myself in that role."</p><p>She has a lot of company. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention recently announced a fertility rate of 1.6 children per American woman — well below the replacement level of 2.1. I'd been brooding on this for a while when the email from a publicist hit my inbox, slugged, "NOV 21: Hit NYC Fringe Show in Chicago — Bailey Swilley's "A Baby For Me? No Thank You, Please!"</p><div class="RichTextSidebarModule Enhancement" data-module data-align-center><a class="AnchorLink" id="module-5b0000" name="module-5b0000"></a> <div class="RichTextSidebarModule-title">Opinion bug</div> <div class="RichTextModule-items RichTextBody"><h2>Opinion</h2></div> </div><p>Approaching random women and asking why they don't want to have children seems a recipe for a quick trip to human resources. But here was an opportunity. About a third of young women don't want kids. What soured Swilley on the prospect?</p><p>"I am an older sister; my brother is five years younger," said Swilley, who grew up in Memphis. "Older enough to remember watching my parents parent him and me, and thinking, 'I don't think that's for me. I just don't see myself in this. Not what I aspire to.'"</p><p>Inherent revulsion to parenthood doesn't usually make the traditional list of reasons people don't want children — jittery economy, lack of suitable partners, the generally fraught future. Swilley mentioned the term "body horror" — she has a routine about a doctor hunting for part of a broken IUD — as well as the "ring of fire," which I thought had to do with volcanic activity in the Pacific, but is also a phrase associated with the pain of childbirth.</p><p>Swilley is married — I assumed her husband is on board with her determined childlessness.</p><p>"We're on the same page," she said. "I bring it up a lot. I ask him. All of his friends have kids, more his friends than mine. We spend a lot of time with his friends' kids. Afterward, I'll check in, 'Did you feel anything? Feel that should be something we do?' We have those check-ins a lot, and always land at 'no.'"</p><p>Other folks' kids will do that. I distinctly remember the shock of being childless and visiting friends who had just had children, to find them sitting sunken-eyed in the middle of their shattered apartments, their padded coffee tables and plastic safety gates and gadgets, spattered with spit-up and splotches of green and orange baby food, smiling these serene, exhausted, souls-among-the-damned-in-hell grins and urging us to follow them over the cliff into their zombie cult.</p><p>I asked Swilley if she worries, having planted her flag so publicly against ever having children, that she may someday change her mind.</p><p>"A lot of women talk about the concept of being John Mulaney," she said. "The comedian John Mulaney was all about 'We never want kids. Me and my wife love our lives, child-free.' Then all of a sudden he left his wife and got this really hot woman pregnant."</p><p>Here she lets out a laugh.</p><p>"Oh my God, you can think you're on the same page, and the rug gets swept out from under you. That's something lurking in a lot of child-free women's minds."</p><p>Well, yes, life will yank that old rug out from under you. I don't think either my wife or I planned on grinding away as mid-60-ish custodians maintaining a decaying 121-year-old, five-bedroom farmhouse with a formal dining room, so it'll be available for the pleasure of children and grandchildren for a few days out of every month. Yet here we are.</p><p>Being a parent is hard work, and not for everybody. Space here is limited, and I can only touch on my conversation with Swilley. If you want to hear more, she's at the <a class="Link" href="https://thedentheatre.com/performances/2026/11/21/a-baby-for-me-no-thank-you-please-the-den-theatre-comedy-club-chicago" target="_blank" >Den Theatre</a>, 1331 N. Milwaukee Ave. on Nov. 21 for two shows, 7 and 9 p.m. </p><p>I asked Swilley if she worried she'd be inspiring audience members not to have children — basically responsible for children not being born into the world.</p><p>"No, I don't think so," she said. "It's not me trying to convince anyone. This is my true belief. I believe it's something that's inherently in you, or not. I was just born with the feeling that it just wasn't for me. A lot of people know deep down whether it's for them or not."</p><p>"Ultimately, you're bringing a stranger into the world," she continued. And I thought, <i>Yeah, but they don't stay a stranger for long ...</i> which is the joy, and the burden.</p>
entries.author: Neil Steinberg

entries.title: White Sox assistant hitting coach Joel McKeithan departing for promotion with Cardinals
entries.summary: <p>Successful MLB offenses have a tendency to lose their assistant hitting coaches.</p><p>After leading the American League in runs scored in 2026, and socking the fifth-most home runs in baseball, the White Sox are indeed losing assistant hitting coach Joel McKeithan. A source confirmed to the Sun-Times the news first reported by FanSided–the Cardinals are hiring the 35-year-old McKeithan to be their lead hitting coach.</p><p>McKeithan has been a lead hitting coach for an MLB team before, coming to the White Sox in 2025 after two years in that role for the Reds. In his two seasons as an assistant hitting coach with the Sox, McKeithan worked under then-hitting coach Marcus Thames in ‘25 and with current lead hitting coach Derek Shomon this past year and regularly earned praise from both.</p><p>“Joel does a really, really good job of staying in touch with [Triple-A hitting coach] Aaron Bray in Charlotte,” Shomon said in June when asked about the team’s success incorporating rookies and call-ups. “Just getting tidbits on guys again–if they are on their way up, or maybe going to be on their way up–just to get us in a position where we're prepared for when they get here.”</p><p>White Sox general manager Chris Getz said last month that he expected to retain the team’s coaching staff for the 2027 season, but losing people to promotions with other clubs is a widely accepted cost of business for fielding a winning team. An MLB.com report indicated Sox bench coach Walker McKinven interviewed for the Mariners manager job that eventually went to Jason Kanzler, and a source confirmed that assistant general manager Josh Barfield interviewed for the Astros GM position that went to Randy Flores.</p><p>“That is what I want here,” Sox hitting director Ryan Fuller said during the season on the prospect of his hitting coaches being poached by other teams. “Where other people recognize the work that's being put in, where players are buying into the system, they're making adjustments, they're getting better. That's a natural part of it, unfortunately.”</p><p>With Shomon still expected to return alongside major league assistant Tony Medina to run the Sox major-league hitting operation, an external hire is internally seen as the most likely remedy for replacing McKeithan.</p>

Benton</a></h5><p>Nestled on the second floor of the Chicago History Museum are three colorful, six-by-eight-foot maps of Austin, North Lawndale and Garfield Park. More than street grids, these maps highlight cultural landmarks, like the famous Buck 50 watch hat and the former Sears Tower, which help define each community.</p><p>For nearly a year, West Side residents Drea Slaughter, Jay Simon and Corey Dooley Johnson, known as the Capstone Clique, partnered with the Chicago History Museum to help their neighbors document and preserve their stories.</p><p>The group set out to answer the question: What would a map look like if the neighborhoods’ residents got to decide what belonged on it?</p><p>Working alongside artist Kent Jones, they created large-scale maps of Austin, North Lawndale and Garfield Park, inviting residents to mark the places that mattered most to them — from family homes to neighborhood chicken spots.</p><p>The result: Three large-scale, rainbow-colored maps now on display in the museum’s permanent exhibition, "Chicago: Crossroads of America," until March 2027.</p><p><a class="Link" href="https://newsletters.suntimes.com/t/t-l-yddhudut-l-hr/" target="_blank" ><b>READ MORE</b></a></p><hr><p></p><h4>YOUR DAILY QUESTION ☕️</h4><p><b>Now that the election is over, political ads will take a hiatus. entries.title: Blackhawks coach Jeff Blashill vows to 'stay steady with what we believe in' amid adversity
entries.summary: <p>FORT LAUDERDALE, Fla. — <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks" target="_blank" >Blackhawks</a> coach Jeff Blashill has become public enemy No. 1 among Hawks fans, who eviscerate his lineups and systems online every day.</p><p>Blashill himself probably isn't scrolling the social-media threads or listening to the podcasts ripping him and his team. For his mental health's sake, one hopes he isn't.</p><p>But he is aware of the league standings. He knows the internally set and proclaimed expectations of improvement this season aren't being met. He has some sense of the mounting pressure, which could potentially <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks/2026/11/03/blackhawks-changes-trip-kyle-davidson-jeff-blashill" >reach a fulcrum</a> during a break in the schedule next week.</p><p>"I'd prefer the word 'urgency' over 'desperate.' I think when people do desperate things, they're usually bad," Blashill said Wednesday. "There's certainly an urgency level. But that hasn't changed. Our urgency level has been high for a while."</p><p>However, he doesn't seem to be letting that urgency affect his decisions or coaching style. Nor is he second-guessing any of the decisions he has made since September.</p><p>"I just haven't really looked and said, 'We should've done this different,'" he said. "You're evaluating all the time, but [it's] more evaluation as to, 'This is done. What can we do moving forward?'</p><p>"That doesn't mean we didn't learn from every day we've gone through with this group. [We] make tweaks where we feel we've needed to make tweaks — without making wholesale changes to approach or systems or things like that, because that lead to mega confusion. There's a balance to it."</p><p>Much of the criticism of Blashill's lineups and systems boils down to one crucial, overarching difference in philosophy.</p><p>Fans expect him to design those based on what would maximize the Hawks' chances of winning games right now. Instead, he's designing them based on how the Hawks will ideally look and play years from now as a contending team.</p><p>He's letting Frank Nazar and Anton Frondell center their own lines — instead of loading them up with each other and/or with Connor Bedard — because, as he has mentioned often, most elite NHL teams have three dangerous lines.</p><p>The current Hawks are far from elite, so they don't have enough talent to form three dangerous lines — especially since all three centers are relatively inexperienced. That leads to Frondell being flanked by uninspiring wingers (Cole Smith and Teuvo Teravainen on Wednesday) while trying to handle matchups against the league's best.</p><p>What's better for Frondell's development: playing with the best possible linemates, or accumulating experience in the long-term role the Hawks foresee for him? Fans seem to think the former; Blashill seems to think the latter.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="Figure-content"><figcaption class="Figure-caption"><p>Jeff Blashill said he isn’t second-guessing his decisions dating back to training camp.</p></figcaption><span class="line"></span><div class="Figure-credit"><p>Anthony Vazquez/Sun-Times</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>It's the same theme with Blashill's systems, which involve pressuring opposing teams aggressively in all three zones. </p><p>The Hawks run a 2-1-2 <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks/2026/10/16/blackhawks-forward-lineup-strategy-forechecking-puck-pressure" >forecheck</a> with not one but two men pursuing the puck, which sometimes leaves the "F3" on an island. They're supposed to step up in the neutral zone instead of trapping at the blue line, too.</p><p>Those tactics work better for fast players than slower players. Some Hawks veteran forwards struggle with it. But the speedy kids fit it well — and more as prospects graduate into the NHL, that speed should become more universal throughout the lineup.</p><p>In the defensive zone, there's a lot of <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks/2026/02/18/blackhawks-nhl-defensive-system-olympics-practice-jeff-blashill" >complexity</a>. The fact the Hawks play man-on-man defense up high (compared to zone down low) and swarm loose or bobbled pucks along the boards puts heavy decision-making pressure on every individual player.</p><p>That often backfires because young players are prone to mistakes. But in theory, the system makes good use of the Hawks' long, agile defensemen. Retreating into a passive box around the net would probably reduce scoring chances against in the short term, but there's a reason most contenders don't play that way.</p><p>One could argue the Hawks need wins to build a winning culture. Perhaps that should come before worrying about the intricacies of their future identity. But Davidson hired Blashill knowing this would be his approach.</p><p>"I do see the benefit of playing a certain system and learning within that rather than playing one way that maybe has training wheels on it," Davidson <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks/2025/11/04/kyle-davidson-encouraged-by-connor-bedard-blackhawks-growing-into-the-league-this-season" >said</a> last November. "You just [say], 'You know what? You guys are NHL players, and you're going to play like the NHL-level team we want to be.' I like that process."</p><p>Hawks players remain on board with it, too.</p><p>"Part of [Blashill's] emphasis is to play fast and hard, and our team is just as fast as any team in the league," Alex Vlasic said Wednesday. "We have a lot of players that are explosive and quick. If we're able to execute defensively and transition the puck and play that fast-and-hard style, it's going to be hard for teams to keep up."</p><p>Vlasic, for the record, also praised Blashill's "passionate" and detail-oriented coaching and added that "it's on us as players...to execute things at a higher percentage."</p><p>It's truly unclear how much runway Blashill has left. The aforementioned urgency could force Davidson to take action soon if results don't improve.</p><p>Blashill is carrying on unfazed, though.</p><p>"An important part of coaching [is] staying steady on the rudder in the midst of challenges," he said. "Certainly we're facing challenges right now, but we've got to stay steady with what we believe in."</p>

entries.title: UIC student arrested, student center evacuated after attempted stabbing on campus
entries.summary: <p>A University of Illinois Chicago student was arrested after an attempted stabbing in the school's student center on Wednesday afternoon, university officials said.</p><p>The stabbing attempt was reported on the second floor of the school's Student Center East, 750 S. Halsted St., Wednesday afternoon. The other student involved wasn't stabbed or injured, according to a UIC spokesperson.</p><p>The student center was evacuated and will be closed while the investigation continues.</p><p>UIC police are investigating. Chicago police referred the Chicago Sun-Times to UIC for information on the incident.</p>

entries.title: Accelerant found where man fatally burned, beaten in Portage Park
entries.summary: <p>Police are trying to find out who set a man on fire and beat him in a homicide early Tuesday outside a Volkswagen dealership in Portage Park on the Northwest Side. </p><p>An accelerant — lighter fluid — was found near the man's body, according to a police report obtained by the Chicago Sun-Times. </p><p>A resident of a home nearby saw the fire and called 911, and officers found the man's body outside City Volkswagen, 5330 W. Irving Park Rd., about 12:10 a.m., according to police and sources. </p><p>The unidentified man suffered burns to his body and head injuries and was dead on the scene, police said. </p><p>No one has been arrested. </p><p>Area 5 detectives are conducting a homicide investigation. </p>
entries.author: Sun-Times Wire

entries.title: Boy, 16, killed in shooting in East Side home
entries.summary: <p>A 16-year-old boy was shot and killed inside a home in the East Side neighborhood Wednesday morning, Chicago police said.</p><p>The unidentified teen was inside a residence in the 9700 block of South Avenue L when he was shot about 7:06 a.m. He was pronounced dead at the scene.</p><p>No one else was injured. </p><p>No one has been arrested, and Area detectives are investigating.</p>
entries.author: Misha Manjuran Oberoi

entries.title: Juliana Stratton’s win marks historic first for women of color in national politics
entries.summary: <p>When U.S. Sen.-elect Juliana Stratton is officially sworn in next January, Illinois will become the first state with two women of color serving in the Senate simultaneously.</p><p>Stratton, Illinois' first Black lieutenant governor, will also become the sixth Black woman to serve in the U.S. Senate and the second from Illinois.</p><p>“We already have Sen. (Tammy) Duckworth fighting in Washington. I’m looking forward to joining her and keeping this going,” Stratton said during an appearance with Gov. JB Pritzker Wednesday. “In Illinois, our values are rooted in compassion for every community and every person. This team, we have your back.”</p><p>During her victory speech Tuesday night, Stratton said outgoing Sen. Dick Durbin had reminded her that the seat she was vying for is the same one Abraham Lincoln and Stephen Douglas had once run against each other for, notably splitting on slavery. She noted her great-great grandfather, William Stephens, was freed when the Emancipation Proclamation was signed. </p><p>So now, “The seat where the future of slavery was once debated will be held by a descendant of someone who was enslaved," she said. </p><p>“That progress was possible because people not only believed things could change, but demanded that they did,” Stratton told her victory party crowd Tuesday night. “It was possible because of the courage of people who refused to accept the limits placed on them. Because of the relentless work to ensure that the next generation would go further than the last. I don’t take the history of this seat lightly, because I know that I did not get here alone.”</p><p>Democratic Party of Illinois Chair Elizabeth Hernandez said in a statement Tuesday that Illinois “remains a trailblazer for broken ceilings in having two powerhouse women of color representing us in the upper chamber," but she also recognized Stratton’s win came amid massive wins for Democrats nationally that brought its <a class="Link" href="https://apnews.com/article/midterm-election-native-american-black-governor-senator-women-93d4d163acfd217521b5dce1ab7fc4a9" target="_blank" ><u>own wave of historic firsts</u></a>.</p><p>Tuesday's election saw the country’s <a class="Link" href="https://apnews.com/article/georgia-governor-lance-bottom-jackson-midterm-election-67c22a38b9a6e4cad5584aa44acf106f" target="_blank" ><u>first Black female governor</u></a>, <a class="Link" href="https://apnews.com/article/new-mexico-governor-haaland-hull-2016748de99c93113899cd1688902c69" target="_blank" ><u>the first Native American female governor</u></a>, the first Native female senator, the <a class="Link" href="https://apnews.com/article/elsayed-michigan-democrats-rogers-stevens-280a81f3edc4608fd7c25388171ba2d4" target="_blank" ><u>first Muslim U.S. senator</u></a><u> </u>and <a class="Link" href="https://apnews.com/article/new-hampshire-senate-sununu-pappas-2b2235cf4d8ca6e0eebd2817bf8767f6" target="_blank" ><u>the first openly gay U.S. senator</u></a>. Alabama elected its first transgender state legislator, and a Black trans woman is headed to the Washington state legislature for the first time next spring as well.</p><p>“America sent a very clear message,” Duckworth said.</p>
entries.author: Violet Miller

entries.title: Gov. JB Pritzker, mum on White House ambition, offers congressional agenda in wake of Dems' blue wave
entries.summary: <p>Declaring Democrats’ sweeping national electoral wins as “a clear mandate” to reverse President Donald Trump’s agenda, Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker on Wednesday laid out 200 policy proposals for his party’s new majorities to pass in Congress and address “the real challenges of everyday people, raise wages and lower costs.”</p><p>The sweeping federal recommendations Pritzker presented the morning after <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/11/03/governor-illinois-jb-pritzker-darren-bailey-collin-corbett-results" target="_blank" ><u>breezing to a rare third term</u></a> could easily be mistaken for a presidential platform.</p><p>But while the billionaire governor and long-speculated 2028 White House hopeful called his “Fighting For Illinois: Day One” agenda “a playbook that will be good for others,” he reiterated his focus is on “the people of the state of Illinois.”</p><p>“This is the day after a monumental election in which the American people have said that Congress must act. We want to make sure that the Congress has an agenda, one that's good for the people of Illinois,” Pritzker said during a West Side news conference alongside Sen. Tammy Duckworth and Lt. Gov. Juliana Stratton, who will be sworn in <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/11/03/us-senate-illinois-midterm-results" target="_blank" ><u>as Illinois’ junior senator</u></a> in January.</p><p>“If it's good for other states, that's great, but I'm concerned about the people of Illinois. That's what I'm focused on,” Pritzker said. “We're sending two of the great fighters that are behind me to Congress to fight for the people of Illinois, and to bring this agenda with them.”</p><p>The 75-page agenda outlines numerous proposals to repeal broad spending cuts authorized in Trump’s “Big Beautiful Bill” that decimated Medicaid coverage, SNAP payments and a litany of other social services.</p><p>It also calls for an end to the war in Iran, passage of universal health care, immigration reform, stringent guardrails around the artificial intelligence industry, codification of abortion rights and raising the minimum wage, among a slew of other suggestions for federal leaders.</p><p>Duckworth interjected when Pritzker was asked whether he saw why observers might interpret the Washington agenda as the precursor to a presidential campaign announcement.</p><p>“The things we have done in Illinois should be a model for the nation,” Duckworth said. “The policies that this governor has put into place in Illinois are the same policies that will be good for the United States… This is not something that just suddenly fell out of the sky, or that the governor wrote last night. This is all stuff that we've been discussing for a very long time, and now it's time to execute them.</p><p>“And yes, if we're going to lead, then let's lead from Illinois,” said Duckworth — who added that if Pritzker runs for president, “I will support him 110%.”</p><p>The governor has bolstered his national political profile since Trump’s return to office, and during his election night victory speech, he zeroed in on the theme of “hope” that starkly echoed the message of another Chicagoan who rose to higher office, former President Barack Obama.</p><p>Pritzker’s on track for his widest margin of victory yet while becoming Illinois’ first Democrat elected to a third term as governor and the first in more than a century to carry McHenry County, the most conservative collar county, as the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/11/04/blue-tsunami-democrats-massive-advantage-illinois-general-assembly" target="_blank" ><u>blue tsunami washed through Springfield</u></a>, too.</p><p>With about 91% of expected votes counted, Pritzker was carrying about 60% of the vote while thumping Republican challenger Darren Bailey’s 37%. The Democrat won his first term by about 16 percentage points over GOP former Gov. Bruce Rauner in 2018, and nearly 13 points over Bailey in 2022.</p><p>Whether his sole focus is on his home state, Pritzker once again sidestepped the question of if, or when, he’ll decide on a White House bid.</p><p>“Everything, including the agenda that we put forward today and everything we've done in the last eight years, has really been about the people of Illinois,” Pritzker said. “What is good for the people of Illinois? Those are the questions that I ask every day. When I wake up in the morning, what am I gonna do to make people's lives better? And I go to bed at night thinking about, what didn't I get done that day that I need to do the next day? Those are the things that’ll guide all the decisions I make going forward.”</p>
entries.author: Mitchell Armentrout

entries.title: Bears coach Ben Johnson has mastered the art of turning the page
entries.summary: <p>If all things were equal, the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a>’ first team meeting of each week would feel the same after a win as it did after a loss. Corrections would be made with impersonal precision.</p><p>That’s not the case, though, inside Halas Hall or anywhere else.</p><p>But Ben Johnson can try.</p><p>“We try to be as consistent as we possibly can and we tell them the truth and it's not about hurting feelings or anything like that,” the Bears coach said Wednesday. “We're all in the business of getting better.”</p><p>That’s as true now — in a week the football-loving world officially fell in love with the Bears after a <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/11/02/bears-seahawks-score-13-9-halftime-monday-night-football-caleb-williams-ben-johnson-physicality-nfl" >34-17 win in Seattle </a>— as it’s been at any point in Johnson’s career. And that's why, even in the minutes after beating the defending Super Bowl champions Monday night, Bears players were hesitant to make any grand declarations about the message they sent to the league.</p><p>“We’re not really focused on everybody else … ” safety Cam Lewis said. “It was just our next game.”</p><p>Said receiver Kalif Raymond: “We’ve still got a lot of season left.”</p><p>And defensive end Montez Sweat: “The tape speaks for itself.”</p><p>They’re channeling a head coach that, in his Bears career, has mastered the art of turning the page — especially after victories. He’s had a lot more experience dealing with wins than losses, too. Johnson has won 68% of his regular season games in a year-and-a-half, the highest percentage by any Bears head coach since George Halas retired in 1967. Amazingly, a win Sunday would push him past Halas and behind only Ralph Jones, who last coached for the Bears in 1932, in franchise annals.</p><p>Johnson hasn’t won this many games without knowing how to get his players to turn the page from week-to-week. He can’t tell his players to ignore the outside world — “We’re in a day and age where everybody sees everything on their cell phones,” he said — but he can encourage them to put zero stock in it.</p><p>“We’ve gotta keep winning,” Johnson said. “We’ve gotta win each and every week. We gotta go 1-0 this week. That’s all we care about. That’s all we’ve talked about for the last year and a half in this building, and that doesn’t change, no matter what our record is and what’s happened previously. We’re gonna go right back to work. We’re gonna prepare just like we’ve been doing.”</p><p>That’s in part how the Bears won four consecutive games last year and then, after a loss, five more in a row. The Bears currently are riding a three-game winning streak, their third stretch with at least that many wins since Johnson’s arrival. Coach Matt Eberflus, by contrast, had one three-game winning streak in almost three seasons.</p><p>Johnson's turn-the-page mantra is not just messaging, either. It’s starts with film study.</p><p>“I believe in the coaching staff, I believe in the players, I believe in our process,” Johnson said. “And our process is one of hard work and belief. That’s what we just continue to hone into.”</p><p>Players naturally take coaching points with a better attitude after wins. It’s human nature.</p><p>But that doesn’t make the corrections any less important.</p><p>“When you win, all the mistakes are minimized,” Johnson said. “And then when you lose, everything gets magnified to the nth degree. But they're still there. Each and every game, there's always things that we've got to clean up and get better at.”</p><p>If anything, Johnson said, he can coach his players harder after wins that he can after losses.</p><p>“And yet, at the same time,” he said, “we try to be as consistent as we possibly can be throughout.”<br></p>

entries.title: Gov. JB Pritzker takes personal pride in Texas Gov. Greg Abbott’s defeat
entries.summary: <p>To Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker, the fight to defeat Texas Gov. Greg Abbott was personal.</p><p>It started in 2021, when Abbott signed into law an abortion ban at six weeks of pregnancy. That led to Pritzker sending letters to corporate executives with ties to Texas, advising them to reconsider doing business in a state that "strips its residents of their dignity." </p><p>Then Abbott opened the floodgates the following year, sending thousands of migrants to Chicago and saying he would continue to do so until then-President Joe Biden secured the border. </p><p>The tension boiled over in January 2024, when the Illinois governor <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/2024/1/12/24036176/pritzker-urges-texas-gov-greg-abbott-to-stop-migrant-dropoffs-amid-winter-storm" target="_blank" >pleaded with the Texas governor to halt migrant drop-offs</a> in the dead of Chicago winter.</p><p>“I plead with you for mercy for the thousands of people who are powerless to speak for themselves,” Pritzker said in a letter. “Please, while winter is threatening vulnerable people’s lives, suspend your transports and do not send more people to our state.”</p><p>And last year, Abbott took center stage in the President Donald Trump-approved battle to net Texas five additional GOP seats. Pritzker responded by <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/politics/2025/08/03/texas-democrats-flee-to-illinois-to-block-trump-backed-gop-redistricting-plan" target="_blank" >taking in 40 Texas House Democrats</a> in August 2025 to deny Republicans a quorum needed to approve the new maps, which could have expanded the state’s GOP congressional majority in the pivotal midterm elections.</p><p>Abbott then sent Texas National Guard troops to Illinois as part of Trump’s Operation Midway Blitz, although the guardsmen were never deployed after a <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/donald-trump/2025/10/22/judges-order-blocking-national-guard-deployment-will-remain-in-effect-for-now-but-all-eyes-on-supreme-court" target="_blank" >protracted court battle</a>.</p><p>Pritzker, the billionaire heir to the Hyatt hotel fortune, responded to all of the ire with his dollars — contributing $1.2 million to Democratic gubernatorial candidate Gina Hinojosa and $100,000 to U.S. Senate candidate James Talarico through the super PAC Lone Star Rising. Pritzker was Hinojosa's second-largest donor, behind only the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee, which gave $1.49 million. Pritzker also <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/illinois-governor/2026/06/23/gov-pritzker-top-chicago-fundraiser-senate-candidate-james-talarico-texas" target="_blank" ><u>hosted a Chicago fundraiser for Talarico</u></a> last year.</p><p>He also gave $25,000 each to the Texas House Democratic Caucus and the Texas House Democratic Party Campaign Committee. And he helped Texas Railroad Commissioner Democratic candidate Don Rosenthal with a $25,000 contribution and gave $10,000 each to Travis County Judge Andy Brown and Bexar County Judge Ron Nirenburg.</p><p>All of the Texas candidates Pritzker supported won on Tuesday night.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" id="image-820000" name="image-820000"></a> <picture data-crop="medium"> <source type="image/webp" width="490" height="275" data-srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/e800c95/2147483647/strip/true/crop/8192x4598+0+433/resize/490x275!/format/webp/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F56%2F96%2F0eeac58f46ebbf7788d9bb61176f%2Ftina-2.jpg 1x,https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/41e5d76/2147483647/strip/true/crop/8192x4598+0+433/resize/980x550!/format/webp/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F56%2F96%2F0eeac58f46ebbf7788d9bb61176f%2Ftina-2.jpg 2x" data-lazy-load="true" srcset="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" /> <source width="490" height="275" data-srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/b0437b4/2147483647/strip/true/crop/8192x4598+0+433/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F56%2F96%2F0eeac58f46ebbf7788d9bb61176f%2Ftina-2.jpg" data-lazy-load="true" srcset="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" /> <img class="Image" alt="Illinois Gov. She's also the first Latina to serve as Texas governor. </p><p>And Talarico flipped the Senate seat in Texas, winning 55.08% to Ken Paxton’s 42.99%. Talarico was among the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/politics/2025/08/18/texas-democrats-illinois-two-week-walkout-gop-remap-greg-abbott" target="_blank" ><u>40 Texas Democrats</u></a> who fled to Illinois to deny Republicans a quorum. While some Texas statehouse races are still too close to call, Democrats also appear to have taken control for the first time since 2003.</p><p>"JB has been touting, 'You have to be a fighter’ and that means fighting and winning. And that means you got to be a killer, and you got to go for the jugular when you need to," a source with direct knowledge of Pritzker's thinking said. "And that is sort of how his team operates. If there's an opportunity for us to take you out after you did horrible things, we're going to take that opportunity.”</p><p>Pritzker found the migrant crisis to be "unfathomable" on a humanitarian level, the source said</p><p>"The idea that you could just ship people in buses without coats, without the right shoes with no communication, to a city that was unequipped and you knew was unequipped to handle them. That was just a level that crossed the line, and we did everything we could to deal with that," the source said. "It helped that Texas had such good candidates, and I think he was the first to really recognize that that is a race that needed to be invested in if we were going to actually take him out."</p><h3>Pritzker PAC wins</h3><p>Pritzker <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/10/23/gov-jb-pritzker-campaign-funding-outreach-democrats-other-states-2028-presidential-run" target="_blank" >doled out nearly $40 million</a> to Democrats and allied causes in the midterm elections — including campaigns for the U.S. House and Senate, attorney general, secretary of state, county judges and state parties in more than a dozen states, as well as ballot fights over abortion rights and redistricting. Pritzker also contributed to Tennessee House candidate Justin J. The governor also contributed to Aaron Ford, the Democrat who flipped the governor's seat in Nevada. </p><p>Pritzker also personally contributed to Hinojosa and Keisha Lance Bottoms' campaigns. entries.title: Bears report: DT Kentavius Street goes on injured reserve
entries.summary: <p>Here's what happened Wednesday at Halas Hall:</p><h3><b>Street out</b></h3><p>Two days after he left Monday's game with a knee injury, defensive tackle Kentavius Street was put on season-ending injured reserve. He started a whopping seven of eight games for the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> this season after signing as a free agent, though he took a backseat to Jeffery Simmons after his arrival last week. Street had one sack, two tackles for loss and nine tackles in eight games.</p><p>The Bears promoted tight end Stephen Carlson from the practice squad to take his spot on the active roster and signed former Northwestern defensive end Earnest Brown IV to the practice squad. Brown, a fifth-round pick of the Rams in 2021, hasn't played in a game in two years. Carlson played Monday night after a standard day-of-game promotion as the Bears back-filled the tight end spot following Cole Kmet's season-ending knee injury. </p><h3>Jones done</h3><p>Left tackle Braxton Jones, who has been on injured reserve with a knee injury, had surgery Tuesday and will miss the rest of the season, Johnson said. He started three games this season after signing a one-year free agent deal.</p>

entries.title: Election officials blame coding error for ballot shortage, long lines at some precincts
entries.summary: <p>Election officials blamed a coding error for causing ballot shortages at several Chicago precincts on Tuesday, forcing people to wait in long lines for touchscreen voting machines.</p><p>The Chicago Sun-Times and other outlets <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/news/2026/11/03/election-day-glitch-leads-to-long-lines-ballot-issues-at-chicago-voting-sites" target="_blank" >reported</a> the issue affected precincts across the city, including at polls at Holstein Park, the 1st Ward and District 4.</p><p>The issue affected "split precincts" that require multiple ballot styles because they contain more than one election district boundary, a spokesperson for the Chicago Board of Elections said in a statement Wednesday.</p><p>The spokesperson said the Board of Elections provided the correct number of total ballots to each precinct, but that an unprecedented "coding error" resulted in "an insufficient quantity of one ballot style ... [and] an oversupply of another ballot style" in some split precincts.</p><p>Election officials said they began printing extra ballots and shipping them as soon as the issue was raised, as well as providing extra electronic voting machines. Precincts stayed open beyond 7 p.m., when polls closed, to accommodate the delays, the spokesperson said.</p><p>The board said it has implemented safeguards to prevent the issue from happening again. The board would not say how many precincts ran out of ballots, but said 38% of precincts required multiple ballot styles.</p><p>"The Chicago Board of Elections apologizes to voters for the error that slowed the lines at certain precincts. We applaud the dedication of the voters who stuck with us through the delay, and we thank them for their patience and fortitude in casting their votes," the spokesperson said.</p>
entries.author: David Struett

entries.title: Super Bowl or bust for the Bears? They're crossing the Rubicon — and there's no turning back
entries.summary: <p>Three things I think I know about the 6-2 <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a>, who, after a <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/11/02/bears-big-plan-coming-together-beautifully-as-34-17-win-over-seahawks-pushes-them-to-best-start-since-2012" target="_blank" >34-17 win in Seattle</a>, just might be the most buzzed-about team in the NFL:</p><p><b>1. They’ve crossed the Rubicon: </b>The fun of last year’s ascent to a division title and the playoffs is far behind them. Concerns about Caleb Williams’ health and the fleeting charm of winning a couple of games with backup quarterbacks are long gone, too. Now that <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/11/03/el-jefe-takes-charge-dt-jeffery-simmons-embraces-role-responsibility-as-new-boss-of-bears-defense" target="_blank" >linchpin defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons is aboard</a>, the Bears no longer face doubts about the readiness of their roster to take on even the mightiest of foes.</p><p>The die is cast, in other words.</p><p>It’s Super Bowl or bust now. And even if that’s slightly overstating matters eight games into a second straight encouraging season, it’s close enough to the Bears’ truth that there’s no turning back.</p><p>When the Bears lost to the Rams in overtime in last season’s divisional round, the disappointment fans felt was subsumed by a prevailing mix of enthusiasm and pride. That sentiment has hardened since — especially over the last three weeks — into something far more urgent. Last year’s team went as far as it had any business going, requiring near-miracles to get there. These Bears, fierce enough to rag-doll the defending-champion Seahawks on enemy turf, are in the mix to win all the marbles and the entire football world can see it.</p><p>But that also means falling short from here will be met with disappointment and worse. There won’t be such a soft spot for the Bears if they back into the playoffs as a wild card, say, or if they lose another playoff game at Soldier Field. Yes, that’s jumping far ahead, but isn’t that how our expectations have shifted?</p><p>In a sense, the fun and games are over. Caesar has mounted his steed and unsheathed his sword. <i>Alea iacta est</i>.</p><p><b>2. They’ll be in first place by Thanksgiving: </b>As long as I’m being pretentious enough to invoke Latin — look, it was one of the only phrases I know — I might as well lay out what’s going to happen over the next couple of weeks for you.</p><p>The Bears will beat the Buccaneers and Saints to get to 8-2. The Vikings will lose to the Bills and Packers to drop to 6-3. The Packers will split with the Patriots and Vikings and be 6-4. And the Lions will beat the Dolphins and Patriots and be 7-2 when the first-place Bears come calling on Thanksgiving Day.</p><p>I’d give you the Bears-Lions final score now, but why spoil the surprise?</p><p><b>3. Their best stat — by far — is 51-19: </b>That represents the cartoonish gap between third-down conversions by the Bears’ offense (51) and third-down conversions allowed by their defense (19). Can a discrepancy that great be maintained? Probably not. But as long as they even come close to approximating that kind of success on third downs, they should live in the “W” column. So far, it’s this season’s version of the 2025 team’s uncanny success in the turnover department.</p><h3><b>Caleb-o-meter: 9 out of 10</b></h3><p>In three games since returning from a hamstring injury, Williams has completed 73.8% of his passes for 860 yards and four touchdowns, with no interceptions. Passer ratings above 100 are his current norm, unthinkable by previous Bears QB standards. If it means anything to you, he’s up to No. 2 in <a class="Link" href="http://nfl.com/" target="_blank" ><u>NFL.com</u></a>’s weekly QB rankings, behind only the Bills’ Josh Allen.</p><p>Williams might have a future in this business, just saying.</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/11/02/bears-grades-seahawks-caleb-williams-jeffery-simmons-luther-burden-jaxon-smith-njigba-chicago-seattle-lumen-nfl" target="_blank" >Bears’ grades are in. How did they do against the Seahawks?</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/11/03/bears-seahawks-34-17-final-score-caleb-williams-i-want-to-make-these-fans-extremely-proud" >Bears QB Caleb Williams: ‘I want to make these fans extremely proud’</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/halas-intrigue/2026/11/03/bears-seahawks-podcast-halas-intrigue" >Halas Intrigue podcast: Bears dominate Seahawks</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p></p><h3><b>Look who’s coming: the Buccaneers</b></h3><p>Said Williams in Seattle, “We are a smashmouth football team. That’s our identity.”</p><p>That will be tested Sunday night at Soldier Field by the Bucs, who have supplanted the Bears at No. 1 in the NFL in rushing (168.6 yards per game) and are No. 1 in rushing differential (88.6 yards). The Bears are second in both categories.</p><p>The Bucs are 3-5 but lately have been unstoppable on the ground, with 582 rushing yards — including a franchise-record 324 Sunday in a win against the Falcons — the last two weeks. Bucky Irving is fourth in the league with 728 yards, and Kenneth Gainwell leads the league in yards after contact (with Irving two spots behind him).</p><p>Right or wrong, the Bucs are touting themselves as a playoff-caliber team, pointing to the combined winning percentages of their first eight opponents (.590) and their remaining nine (.433, including the Bears). They’re the only team in the weak NFC South with a positive points differential (plus-27).</p><p>Wild prediction: Quarterback Baker Mayfield will have even more success throwing the ball against the Bears than he did in the 16-0 shutout of the Falcons. Under buckets of rain, he attempted all of three passes, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/nfl/2026/11/01/buccaneers-falcons-zero-completions-bears-next-opponent" >completing none.</a></p><h3><b>History department</b></h3><p>With three catches Sunday, Colston Loveland will pass Greg Olsen for the second-most receptions by a Bears tight end in his first two seasons. Loveland — with 20 grabs and 28 targets since Williams’ return — is up to 91, having long since justified the Bears’ drafting him at No. 10 overall. Easily in range this season is Mike Ditka’s Bears record of 114 receptions in 1961 and 1962.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr">Colston Loveland working the scramble drill and getting that knee down. Textbook. 👀 <a href="https://t.co/BVDReLGeP8">pic.twitter.com/BVDReLGeP8</a></p>— Clay Harbor (@clayharbs82) <a href="https://x.com/clayharbs82/status/2117429196490244350?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">November 3, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p></p>
